codeReview.summary: The commit delivers basic `flux tool list` / `flux tool call` behavior and exercises generic-only tool calls, but it does not fully satisfy the assigned feature scope. The CLI runner is wired by dynamically importing the built MCP server artifact instead of a peer shared-runtime seam, and the added coverage never validates a tool that already has a first-class CLI wrapper even though that was part of the feature contract.

issues.description: `defaultToolRuntime` hard-codes a runtime import of `../../../flux-mcp/dist/index.js`. That means `flux tool list` and `flux tool call` only work if the sibling MCP package has already been built and remains at that relative path; `fluxos-cli` itself does not declare or enforce that dependency. This breaks the standalone CLI package boundary and makes the generic runner fail in an independent `fluxos-cli` build or packaged install.

The assigned feature required coverage for tools both with and without first-class CLI wrappers, but this commit never exercises a tool that actually has a first-class CLI surface. The test explicitly uses `flux_get_state` as a tool that only 'maps to a future first-class command', so the first-class-wrapper case remains unimplemented and unverified for VAL-TOOL-002 / the feature description.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The worker had to replace the documented `jq`-based feature inspection step with a Python fallback because `jq` is not installed in this environment. The startup procedure should document a non-`jq` fallback so workers do not burn time on a missing tool.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Handoff `skillFeedback.deviations` says the worker switched to Python after the suggested `jq` command failed; the transcript skeleton also shows the initial `jq` command attempt followed by a Python-based metadata read.

summary: Fail. The feature adds the basic generic runner surface, but the reviewed commit still depends on `flux-mcp/dist` at runtime and does not actually cover a tool with an existing first-class CLI wrapper, so the assigned scope is not fully met.
